name: showreel-fc02-sum-text

voice.text: Why does sum skip some of your numbers? Look at the edges: these ones hug the left. They're stored as text, and sum ignores text. Wrap the range: sum product, two minus signs. The double minus turns text into numbers. Now every row counts.

caption:
Why does SUM skip some of your numbers? 🔢

Look at the edges. Numbers sit on the right of a cell, text on the left. A number pasted from a bank export, a form or a web page often arrives as text that only looks like a number, and SUM ignores text in a range, so the total comes up short with no error.
Fix: =SUMPRODUCT(--B2:B6). The double minus turns each value into a real number before it is added, so every row counts. Works in Excel and Google Sheets. (A cell with real words in it, like "n/a", gives #VALUE!; clean those first.)
Save it for your next budget sheet.

sources.note: SUM: text in a referenced range is ignored
SUMPRODUCT: multiplies and sums arrays; an array operation such as --range is evaluated element by element
Numbers stored as text: left-aligned, not used in calculations
